messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: serving-runtime node gpu-12 reported repeated container crashes (OOM -> CUDA illegal memory access). auto-escalation to #incidents. trace_id=tr-9a3b
jamie: seeing the alert, grabbing triage. what services affected?
priya: looks like model-serving-prod-3 on gpu-12 and gpu-13 started OOM swaps ~10:02 and then CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at 10:04. customers with heavy batch inference impacted (latency spikes + 500 errors).
mateo: adding logs from the node: ```dmesg | tail -n 60
[14432.564] gpu0: kernel: pagewalk: invalid device address at 0x7f8a9c000
[14432.565] gpu0: kernel: cuda: illegal memory access in thread 0x2a7f
[14432.567] containerd: container runtime panic: segfault (SIGSEGV)
```
alexw: stack traces suggest a race in the loader during KV cache refills; seeing repeated pagewalk faults then container restart loop.
samir: what's the node status? can we cordon/drain without customer impact?
priya: node gpu-12 currently 88% mem used, gpu-13 76%. pods on those nodes are critical model-serving. If we cordon+drain they will reschedule to other nodes -> risk spike elsewhere. Might be ok if we throttle traffic first.
jamie: plan proposal: 1) enable canary fallback routing to smaller-quantized model for production traffic 2) cordon gpu-12, run live kernel collect on gpu-13 3) if reproduction confirmed, take affected node out of rotation and escalate to eng-runtime for hotpatch
mateo: preferring to spin up replacement instances in the same pool (dedicated capacity) and move traffic over. ops-bot, can you spin two replacement nodes in pool-prod-gpu A?
ops-bot: @mateo request acknowledged. Spinning 2 replacement nodes in pool-prod-gpu A. Estimated ready in 6m.
customer-sre: FYI customers a,b,c have open requests reporting 5xxs. Preparing a short incident notice if we need a prolonged mitigation.
priya: quick mitigation implemented: rolled routing policy to route 40% traffic to quant-8bit variant (model-lite-v2). Initial error rate drops ~60% for affected customers.
jamie: good. while replacements come up, we should capture repro steps and full kernel oops. Mateo, can you run repro on a staging node with same kernel/drivers? Keep tracing on.
mateo: trying repro now. reproducer script: ```python3 repro.py --model big-bert --batch 32 --seed 42``` started, will tail `/var/log/kern.log` and nvidia-smi.
[...]
mateo: repro triggered similar pagewalk fault in staging. Kernel oops includes: `smmu: pagewalk returned misaligned pte` and GPU trace shows `address=0x7f8a9c000 alignment=8` mismatch.
alexw: that points to a kernel/driver corner where page size alignment differs after eviction. Could be race between eviction and pointer update. Sending logs to eng-runtime.
jamie: eng-runtime, please triage: suspect race in pagewalk when handling async eviction + KV cache refill. Prioritize kernel/driver combo: nvidia-driver 535.86 + kernel 6.1. Ops: which nodes have that combo?
ops-bot: Nodes gpu-12/gpu-13/gpu-21 currently on driver 535.86 + kernel 6.1. gpu-14 already on 540.x.
samir: temporary policy: enable fallback to gpu-14 pool for live traffic, throttle batch sizes to 8 for affected customers, and disable auto-burst for dedicated pools until root cause found. Jamie, can you approve?
jamie: approved. Priya, post short customer update: 1) we saw CUDA illegal memory access causing container restarts on some GPU nodes, 2) we routed traffic to smaller model and different pool to restore throughput, 3) we're investigating root cause and will follow up with timeline.
priya: posting now to affected customers. message: "We're seeing intermittent CUDA illegal memory access on some GPU nodes causing 5xx errors. We've routed traffic to a smaller model and moved workloads to alternate capacity to reduce impact. We're continuing investigation and will update in 60 minutes"
customer-sre: customer A confirmed reduced 5xxs after fallback. still seeing rare latency blips.
mateo: eng-runtime suggests a targeted kernel module toggle to add additional checks in the driver; they want a full coredump and kernel oops for analysis before applying. I've collected vmcore and pushed to internal bucket: gs://redwood-bugbash/tr-9a3b/vmcore.tgz
alexw: forensics note: reproducer reproduces ~1/10 runs. timing-sensitive. We'll instrument with ftrace and a lightweight mutator to increase hit rate.
samir: operational action items: - keep gpu-12 cordoned - continue replacements - keep routing fallback at 40% until eng-runtime gives green - prepare rollback plan if replacements see same faults
jamie: agreed. On-call handoff in 1 hour to @priya. Priya, you'll have the incident lead unless eng-runtime needs immediate escalation.
priya: got it. I'll handle handoff and maintain customer comms. Also scheduling a 2pm deep-dive with eng-runtime and infra to triage kernel-driver interactions.
ops-bot: replacement nodes ready and added to pool-prod-gpu A at 10:18. Rescheduled pods off gpu-12.
mateo: removed dev/test label and re-ran repro on replacement node -> no repro after 20 runs. Good signal but not conclusive.
jamie: closing real-time mitigation loop: routing fallback + replacements appear to have stabilized error rate to baseline. Keeping thread open for root cause. If anyone sees fresh illegal access on other nodes, ping here and escalate to eng-runtime immediately. :white_check_mark:
priya: last update to customers sent at 10:25. We'll post a postmortem draft once eng-runtime provides RCA.
incident-bot: incident tr-9a3b status -> mitigated (partial). next steps: RCA, kernel/driver patch, verify on canary fleet, postmortem within 72h."
